## centering

### CENTERING_BACK_LENIENCY_001

Back centering is held to a materially looser tolerance than the front.

- evidence: `objective`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_014 PSA published grading standards (psacard.com/gradingstandards), transcribed at knowledge/psa/grading-standards.md - Grade Definitions, GEM-MT PSA 10 · lesson_008 web_f4e13adb5cc1 01:30-01:40

### CENTERING_BORDERLESS_001

On a card with no borders, off-centering is not automatically grade-limiting.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_002 yt_t28rOSnMcck 05:11-05:41

### CENTERING_BORDERLESS_COMPARISON_001

For a borderless card, judge centering by comparing against the same card already graded PSA 10 rather than by measuring borders.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_007 yt_ZWtFU4gG8e0 09:50-10:20

### CENTERING_NO_OVERMEASURE_001

Do not distinguish near-centred ratios such as 51/49; if the borders look even, treat the centering as passing.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_008 web_f4e13adb5cc1 02:20-02:35

### CENTERING_PRODUCT_LENIENCY_001

PSA extends centering leeway to products known to be cut off-centre, and withholds it on products known to be well cut; the same off-centre measurement can pass on one product and fail on another.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_008 web_f4e13adb5cc1 03:50-04:20

### CENTERING_PSA10_EVIDENCE_001

Two PSA-slabbed copies of the same card (2020 Panini Prizm #258 Anthony Edwards Silver Prizm) received MINT 9 and GEM MT 10; the 9 shows a visibly wider left border than right while the 10's borders are even.

- evidence: `objective`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_008 web_f4e13adb5cc1 01:43-01:55

### CENTERING_PSA10_STANDARD_002

PSA's published tolerance for a Gem Mint 10 is approximately 55/45 on the front and 75/25 on the reverse, stated as a tolerance not to exceed those figures rather than as an exact cutoff.

- evidence: `objective`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_014 PSA published grading standards (psacard.com/gradingstandards), transcribed at knowledge/psa/grading-standards.md - Grade Definitions, GEM-MT PSA 10

## corners

### CORNERS_COLORED_001

A coloured corner reveals chipping more readily than a white corner, because a white corner cannot show whitening against its own colour.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_009 web_a380d07b6b03 01:00-01:20

### CORNERS_DEFECT_FREQUENCY_001

Corner defects occur in this descending order of frequency: whitening/chipping, then rounding, then bending.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_009 web_a380d07b6b03 00:45-00:55

### CORNERS_FOUR_SHARP_002

PSA describes a Gem Mint 10 as having four perfectly sharp corners.

- evidence: `objective`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_014 PSA published grading standards (psacard.com/gradingstandards), transcribed at knowledge/psa/grading-standards.md - Grade Definitions, GEM-MT PSA 10

### CORNERS_MINOR_TOUCH_COSTS_TEN_002

A single small white touch on one corner can be enough to lower a card from PSA 10 to PSA 9.

- evidence: `objective`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_014 yt_E9do7O74zM0 00:46-01:20

### CORNERS_ROUNDED_002

A corner that shows white and appears rounded is corner wear and counts against the grade.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_002 yt_t28rOSnMcck 02:36-03:07

### CORNERS_THICK_002

Thick cards, such as patch or premium products, damage at the corners more easily than standard stock.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_009 web_a380d07b6b03 02:12-02:19

### CORNERS_TOUCH_001

A corner that appears rounded, raised, or touched holds a card back from a PSA 10.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_001 yt_s46CrXjVwCc 05:11-05:22

## edges

### EDGES_CLEAN_001

Edges should run straight and clean around the whole card; chipping or nicking is a grade-limiting defect.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_001 yt_s46CrXjVwCc 05:22-05:36

### EDGES_COLORED_001

A coloured edge reveals whitening; a white edge cannot show it.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_010 web_9e1801890111 00:20-00:35

### EDGES_JAGGED_001

A jagged or rough-cut edge is an edge defect distinct from whitening.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_005 yt_W02Wvtq89IM 03:05-03:25

### EDGES_NO_ROUNDING_001

Edges do not round or bend the way corners do; whitening is effectively the only edge defect to look for.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_010 web_9e1801890111 00:35-00:55

### EDGES_WHITENING_002

Whitening visible along a card edge is edge wear and counts against the grade.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_002 yt_t28rOSnMcck 02:36-03:07 · lesson_010 web_9e1801890111 00:20-00:35

## image_limitations

### IMAGE_LIMITATIONS_DIMPLE_001

A dimple presents differently in a scan than in person, so its scanned appearance must be recognised as a distinct signature.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_001 yt_s46CrXjVwCc 05:36-05:56

### IMAGE_LIMITATIONS_PSA_SURFACE_001

PSA characterises surface flaws as potentially difficult to see with the naked eye.

- evidence: `objective`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_013 yt_E9do7O74zM0 00:26-00:47

### IMAGE_LIMITATIONS_REQUEST_PHOTOS_001

When listing photographs cannot resolve whether an edge is chipped or a surface mark is real, the correct response is to request more photographs rather than assume.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_006 yt_aA8soPXmsS4 03:58-04:18

### IMAGE_LIMITATIONS_SURFACE_001

Surface defects frequently cannot be assessed from listing photographs; a card may carry a surface flaw that the listing images do not reveal.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_001 yt_s46CrXjVwCc 05:36-05:56 · lesson_011 web_a215e0e689d0 00:05-00:20

## process

### PROCESS_BACKLIGHT_ZOOM_001

Inspect corners by backlighting the card and zooming on each of the four corners in turn.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_004 yt__CjZMweRBdM 06:06-06:27

### PROCESS_CHECKLIST_001

Inspect in a fixed order - centering, corners, edges, surface - then repeat the whole pass on the back.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_003 yt_38QhtEziAx4 02:59-03:20

### PROCESS_PSA_FOUR_CATEGORIES_001

PSA graders primarily assess four attributes: centering within the borders, corner sharpness, surface imperfections, and edge condition.

- evidence: `objective`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_013 yt_E9do7O74zM0 00:26-00:47

## surface

### SURFACE_CLEANABLE_001

Some light surface marks are cleanable before submission, so a visible light mark is not necessarily a permanent grade limit.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_011 web_a215e0e689d0 00:20-00:35

### SURFACE_GEM_REFERENCE_001

A gem-mint reference card shows sharp corners and edges with no whitening anywhere on front or back.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_002 yt_t28rOSnMcck 06:46-07:16

### SURFACE_GLOSS_FOCUS_002

PSA describes a Gem Mint 10 as having sharp focus and full original gloss.

- evidence: `objective`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_014 PSA published grading standards (psacard.com/gradingstandards), transcribed at knowledge/psa/grading-standards.md - Grade Definitions, GEM-MT PSA 10

### SURFACE_NO_STAINING_001

A PSA Gem Mint 10 must be free of staining of any kind.

- evidence: `objective`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_013 PSA published grading standards (psacard.com/gradingstandards) - Grade Definitions, GEM-MT PSA 10

### SURFACE_PRINT_ALLOWANCE_002

PSA may allow a slight printing imperfection on a Gem Mint 10 at its discretion, where the imperfection does not impair the card's overall appeal.

- evidence: `objective`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_014 PSA published grading standards (psacard.com/gradingstandards), transcribed at knowledge/psa/grading-standards.md - Grade Definitions, GEM-MT PSA 10

### SURFACE_PRINT_LINE_BACK_001

Print lines on the back of a card have still received PSA 10 grades.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_003 yt_38QhtEziAx4 01:45-02:11

### SURFACE_PRINT_LINE_PROMINENT_001

A prominent print or factory line running across the face of a card is grade-limiting and is not covered by PSA's slight-imperfection allowance.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_011 web_a215e0e689d0 01:10-01:25 · lesson_014 PSA published grading standards (psacard.com/gradingstandards), transcribed at knowledge/psa/grading-standards.md - Grade Definitions, GEM-MT PSA 10

### SURFACE_SHINY_001 _(card types: chrome, refractor, foil)_

Shiny, foil and refractor-style surfaces scratch more easily and are harder to assess than plain stock.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_011 web_a215e0e689d0 00:35-01:00

### SURFACE_TECHNICAL_DEFECT_001

A grade may be lowered by a technical defect such as a minor crease or paper loss on the back even when the card has strong eye appeal.

- evidence: `objective`  
- confidence: `medium`  
- sources: lesson_013 yt_E9do7O74zM0 01:30-01:40

### SURFACE_THREE_DEFECTS_001

The three surface defects to inspect for are factory/print lines, dimples, and scratches.

- evidence: `experience_based`  
- confidence: `high`  
- sources: lesson_011 web_a215e0e689d0 01:00-01:50
